title: Checking spill reductions and prioritising overflow investigations
summary: I combined six years of storm-overflow returns, checked the 2025 figures and developed maintenance and investigation lists. I used rainfall and monitoring coverage to assess how confidently the fall in recorded spills could be interpreted.
scenario_note: The public datasets, analysis and exported lists are real. The meeting, stakeholder roles and proposed follow-up actions are simulated to demonstrate how I would handle an internal performance brief. I did not work for Severn Trent or submit its regulatory return.
brief: During an annual wastewater performance review, I was asked to check the monitoring return, explain the reduction in recorded spills and identify sites for maintenance or further investigation. I first separated the reporting decision from the operational decision: explaining the annual figures requires different evidence from approving work at a specific site.
requirements_intro: I used my requirements framework to define the measures, comparison periods, data checks and intended users. The analysis produces a performance pack and review lists. Engineering assessment, environmental risk and scheme costs would be needed before investment could be approved.
requirements_summary: Recorded spills fell sharply, but rainfall, monitor availability and changes in the reporting population could affect the comparison.
Do the annual figures reconcile? How much context does rainfall provide? Which monitors need attention? Which high-spill sites report no improvement action?
Support a clear performance report and give maintenance, operations and asset-planning teams specific records to investigate.
Environment Agency annual returns for 2020–2025, Midlands rainfall and a 2025 Excel performance pack. No spill volumes, event-level rainfall, scheme costs or measured environmental benefits.

requirements_template.intro: These prompts show how I would establish the brief with service owners. The status labels distinguish completed analysis from assumptions and decisions needing internal confirmation.

items.prompt: Who needs the findings, and which decisions can this evidence support?
items.application: The Head of Wastewater Performance needs an annual report. Maintenance needs monitor faults; Operations and Asset Planning need high-spill review lists. These stakeholder interactions are simulated.

items.prompt: Which units, periods and asset populations make the comparison interpretable?
items.application: Use counted spills and duration, annual rainfall and monitor operation. Keep the full annual return, the ≥90%-operation comparison and the three-year linked panel distinct. A spill count is not a volume or a direct measure of environmental damage.

items.prompt: Which operational records would confirm the public return and support action?
items.application: Request monitor downtime and fault logs, asset commissioning records, site-level rainfall and improvement-work status from their owners. Only public annual returns and regional rainfall are available here.

items.prompt: Which checks block reporting, and how will unresolved exceptions be explained?
items.application: The workbook records duplicate-ID, value-range and consistency checks separately from items needing review. Missing spill counts, changed asset IDs and large increases remain owner-confirmation tasks; the pack is not a signed-off regulatory submission.

items.prompt: Which adjustments are useful, and where could they mislead?
items.application: Use a ≥90% monitor-operation threshold and compare years with similar annual rainfall. A five-observation rainfall model provides exploratory context only. Its adjusted priority list is separate from the observed 2025 high-spill list.

items.prompt: What would make an exception actionable, and which response target applies?
items.application: Start with repeat monitor problems and high-spill sites reporting no improvement action. Confirm current fault and programme status, environmental urgency, owner and response time. The analytical 90% and 60-spill thresholds are not contractual service-level agreements (SLAs) or automatic investment approvals.

items.prompt: Which deliverables and checks are needed before the report is used?
items.application: Provide an Excel pack, clear definitions, validation results and separate review lists. Agree a reporting deadline, sign-off responsibilities and exception-resolution criteria with the actual service owners. No internal approval or delivered improvement is claimed.

data_requests: Check counted spills, duration and monitor operation by asset and year.
Public Environment Agency annual returns; no event-level telemetry.
Confirm active assets, repeat failures, repairs and changes in identifiers.
Published IDs and low-operation reasons; no internal work orders.
Assess weather context and investigate site-level differences.
Public Met Office Midlands annual rainfall; no matched local storm data.
Confirm work status, feasibility and investment options.
Published reporting-period activity descriptions; no budgets or business cases.
data_intro: Inside the organisation, I would request monitoring extracts, fault histories and programme records from their owners, then agree asset identifiers and reporting cut-offs. For this project, I used the public annual returns and rainfall series. I kept missing spill counts separate from genuine zero-spill records.
actions: Review the 27 repeat low-operation records first, then assess the remaining maintenance exceptions. Confirm the fault is still active before raising work.
Agreed fault owner, diagnosis and response target; track repeat faults and recovered monitor availability.
Review the 13 observed high-spill sites reporting no improvement action. Check investigation status, local conditions and the current work programme before selecting interventions.
A verified site-level explanation and an agreed next step, supported by engineering and environmental evidence.
Reconcile the 21 missing spill counts, 11 new IDs, 18 removed IDs and two large increases before formal reporting.
Each review item resolved or qualified in an approved exception log, with clear denominators.
Validate the longer-term screening with local rainfall and event-level data; test sensitivity to the rainfall adjustment and screening thresholds.
A documented assessment of whether site priorities remain stable under alternative assumptions.
